rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation of the skip rules; project retained; equivalence argued, not proved. The worksheet says to skip lines 23–43 when lines 1 and 16 are the same, lines 33–43 when lines 1 and 32 are the same, lines 35–40 when Schedule D line 19 is zero or blank, and lines 41–43 when Schedule D line 18 is zero or blank (i1040sd pp. 15–16, Schedule D Tax Worksheet). The project encodes each skip as a zero-valued alternative on every skipped line; the second transcription computes every line unconditionally and treats a skipped line as blank only where a later line reads it. The two agree in value when the skipped lines are zero anyway: with lines 1 and 16 equal, line 17 equals line 1 less line 13 and line 22 equals line 13, so lines 25 and 29, hence 30–34, are zero; with Schedule D line 19 zero, line 35 and so 39–40 are zero; with Schedule D line 18 zero, line 42 is the remainder of line 1 after the ordinary, 0%, 15%, 20% and 25% portions (lines 21, 22, 30, 33, 39) and is zero. That argument is recorded here, not machine-checked; it is a candidate property for the data-level property tests of spec 6.3 (a skipped line evaluates to zero under the project's reading and under unconditional computation). No change to the data.
